figures.caption: Fig. 1 Conditional dependency graph of the framework. Nodes represent definitions, constructions, or results. A directed edge indicates logical prerequisite.

Fig. 2 Hardness / obstruction regime diagram. Projection hardness Ha→b(ε) and sheaf-Laplacian obstruction Ca→b(ε) capture two orthogonal failure modes of cross-modal alignment. Low hardness and low obstruction indicate compatibility; high hardness indicates insufficient global expressivity; high obstruction indicates locally valid alignments that cannot be glued into a coherent global map.

Fig. 3 Each node corresponds to a sample in the modality-independent site G, with a parameter vector wv attached at each vertex. Left: a constant parameter field corresponding to a single global map. Middle: a smoothly varying field with low sheaf-Laplacian energy (low obstruction). Right: a sharply varying field with large energy concentrated across a cut, illustrating obstruction despite perfect local fits.
